title: A Study to Establish the Diagnostic Value of the EPISEEK-MPE Liquid Biopsy Assay to Identify Cancer in Pleural Effusion Samples.
official: Development of a Molecular Assay to Diagnose Malignant Pleural Effusions
summary:
The goal of this study is to evaluate the EPISEEK-MPE laboratory test for diagnosis of malignant (cancerous) pleural effusions verses pleural effusions caused by a non-cancer condition. The study uses excess samples drained from around the lung as part of a patient's regular care. The main questions the study aims to answer are:

1. Is the EPISEEK-MPE test reliable to detect cancer cells and aid in the diagnosis of malignant pleural effusions?
2. Do age, race, gender and ethnicity change the reliability of the EPISEEK-MPE test?
3. Can the results of the EPISEEK-MPE test predict which patients have a better chance of survival than others?

Participants will be asked to donate a small portion of the excess fluid drained from around the lung for research. Participants will also give permission to collect data from the medical records.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adult patients having pleural fluid drained for clinical care (thoracentesis or chest tube placement)
* Consent to have pleural fluid sample used for research

Exclusion Criteria:

\- Insufficient fluid available following clinical drainage procedure
